key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion promote dense Fe-based amorphous coatings, while greater porosity reduces long-term corrosion resistance and higher humidity lowers friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray parameters and accounting for service humidity can support corrosion- and wear-resistant coatings on Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with higher porosity and decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear results involve Si3N4 counterface balls and may not generalize to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
